pr_title: Add option to FIPS module to enforce EMS check during KDF TLS1_PRF
pr_body:
Fixes #19989

The check is disabled by default.
It can be enabled via fipsinstall using '-ems_check'
~~It can be removed from openssl config using 'no-fips-ems_check'~~

To detect its use inside the TLS_PRF it looks at the label.. If the label is 'mastersecret' then the check fails.
TLS1_PRF is used multiple times for other purposes, so if we need to pass it as a param then it may need multiple params passed.

issue_context.title: Add support for mandating use of EMS in TLS 1.2
issue_context.body:
[FIPS 140-3 Implementation Guidance](https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/documents/fips%20140-3/FIPS%20140-3%20IG.pdf) requires that only EMS KDF in TLS 1.2 can be used with modules validated after May 16, 2023 (see "D.Q Transition of the TLS 1.2 KDF to Support the Extended Master Secret").

Please add a setting that would enable and _require_ negotiation of EMS extension for TLS 1.2 connections. That setting then could default to enabled when operating in FIPS mode.
comments: Is there a reason to not require EMS unconditionally?
@tomato42 then OpenSSL should disable DHE and RSA key exchange unless EMS is used.  Otherwise 3SHAKE works.
**OTC: We are OK with adding this feature off by default to 3.1 before the final release.**
Confounding concern: technical enforcement for FIPS purposes needs to be done inside the provider boundary.  It's not sufficient to force it from libssl.
@paulidale Yes, but on TLS level, the correct time to reject it is right after receiving ClientHello (or right after receiving ServerHello that doesn't advertise EMS).

Agreed.  Another FIPS oddity being born.

You have to enforce X even though it's never possible to encounter X.
@paulidale The change I have done here is at the KDF level, not the TLS level.

Those patches seem to be just about the KDF calculation, I was asking for ability to control extension negotiation...

Could I get this issue re-opened? Or should I file a new one?

I've reopened this issue.

Note that, from a FIPS perspective (which is where this mandate comes from), the fix **must** be inside the FIPS boundary.  For us, the KDF calculation is the only place where this is possible.  Putting an equivalent fix into libssl doesn't meet the FIPS requirements -- it's not inside the boundary.

I know you define your boundary differently, so a libssl fix might be applicable.
Apart from suggesting how this would be done, I dont see this is actually relevant for the OpenSSL validation.

It isn't relevant to the OpenSSL validations.

It's something we'd probably want in libssl too.  As noted [above](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/19989#issuecomment-1421694650), that's the sensible place for such a check.

Yes, for FIPS validation the fix needs to be inside the validated module boundary, so `fips.so`.
But from UX point of view, additional check should be in libssl. Also, as pointed out [earlier](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/19989#issuecomment-1370340993), it's useful for ensuring that the connection isn't vulnerable to 3SHAKE attack, even when not in FIPS mode.
@tomato42 not only useful, but essential.  Otherwise there is a security vulnerability.
Do we have anything else to do here?

@paulidale sorry, but I don't think the linked PR https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20241 addresses the reason why we re-opened this ticket: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/19989#issuecomment-1460705997
